q: Water can also dissociate into hydrogen and hydroxide ions, and the process is known as ____.
e: Water can also dissociate into hydrogen and hydroxide ions, and the process is known as autoionisation. Autoionisation: water autoionises when two H2O molecules make H3O+ and OH-.

q: The number of hydrogen ions that water will receive, determines the ____, which is related to hydrogen ion concentration.
e: The number of hydrogen ions that water will receive, determines the pH, which is related to hydrogen ion concentration. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: Although water is a very weak electrolyte and a poor conductor of electricity, it undergoes ____ to a small extent.
e: Although water is a very weak electrolyte and a poor conductor of electricity, it undergoes ionisation to a small extent. Ionisation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In pure water, one $H_2O$ molecule donates a proton and acts as an ____, and another water molecule accepts a proton and acts as a base at the same time.
e: In pure water, one H2O molecule donates a proton and acts as an acid, and another water molecule accepts a proton and acts as a base at the same time. Acid is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Having both proton-accepting (protophilic) and proton-donating (protogenic) properties, water is called an ____ molecule.
e: Having both proton-accepting (protophilic) and proton-donating (protogenic) properties, water is called an amphiprotic molecule. An amphiprotic species can both donate a proton and accept a proton.

q: $K_w$ is called the ____ of water which is the product of the molar concentrations of $H^+$ and $OH^-$ ions at a particular temperature.
e: Kw is called the ionic product of water which is the product of the molar concentrations of H+ and OH- ions at a particular temperature. Kw is the ionic product of water, [H+][OH-], and it equals 1.0 x 10^-14 at 25 degrees Celsius.

q: From the measurement of the electrical conductance of pure water, it was found that the concentration of ionised ion was ____.
e: From the measurement of the electrical conductance of pure water, it was found that the concentration of ionised ion was 1.0 x 10-7 mol dm-3. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: In pure water, the concentration of $H^+$ ion is always ____ to the concentration of $OH^-$ ion.
e: In pure water, the concentration of H+ ion is always equal to the concentration of OH- ion. Equal: higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: If the individual concentration of hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions in an aqueous solution is equal to $1.0 \times 10^{-7} mol dm^{-3}$ at $25^\circ C$ (298 K), the solution is called a ____ solution.
e: If the individual concentration of hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions in an aqueous solution is equal to 1.0 x 10-7 mol dm-3 at 25degreesC (298 K), the solution is called a neutral aqueous solution. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Since the process of autoionisation is ____, the concentrations of hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions increase with temperature.
e: Since the process of autoionisation is endothermic, the concentrations of hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions increase with temperature. The system gains heat, so delta H is positive.

q: The ____ to base 10 of the molar concentration of hydrogen ions is used to calculate the pH.
e: The negative logarithm to base 10 of the molar concentration of hydrogen ions is used to calculate the pH. Negative logarithm: pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: Similarly, pOH is the negative logarithm to base 10 of the molar concentration of the ____ ions.
e: Similarly, pOH is the negative logarithm to base 10 of the molar concentration of the hydroxide ions. pOH is the negative log of the hydroxide-ion concentration.

e: At 298 K, the value of Kw is 1.0 x 10-14 mol2 dm-6, and so, pH + pOH = 14. The f subshell holds fourteen electrons after s, p, and d take 2, 6, and 10.

e: Acids have pH values of less than 7. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

e: For acids, the smaller the pH value (the higher the concentration of H+ ions), the stronger the acid is. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.
